project_announced_description: This Rural Development loan guarantee investment will be used to finance the construction and operation of 3MW Gasification Plant. The plant will convert forestry biomass waste into a synthetic natural gas through the process of thermochemical conversion. The project is located in Wilseyville, CA (Calaveras County). There is also a pending grant application that has already been approved by the Efficiency Team (guaranteed loan package had not been submitted at that time). The purpose of the award is for the construction of the plant. Annual operating expenses are estimated to start at $3.2 million in the first year of operations and gradually increase to $4.1 million by year 20. This award will provide funds for the initial working capital to pay expenses during the first year. Total project costs for the construction of the plant are estimated to be $42.2 million. USDA funds will account for $25 million, while the borrower will contribute the balance from other sources of funds: subordinated debt ($12 million), grants ($5.1 million), cash injection $186 thousand). The $25 million in USDA funding will be used for: construction costs ($19,260,430); Working Capital ($336,095); construction interest reserve ($2,865,369); debt service reserve ($1,621,000); and closing costs ($917,106).

project_name: 2019 Well Replacement & Water Plant Improvement Project
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to install approximately 4,100 feet of eight inch polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sewer main and install manholes along Monroe Street near the Torres-Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indian Reservation in southwestern Riverside County. The new eight inch sewer main will be connected to an existing 33-inch sewer main, owned and operated by the Coachella Valley Water District (CVWD). The new sewer main will connect a subdivision, church, and community building located within the Torres-Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indian Reservation to the existing sewer collection system operated by CVWD. The housing units and facilities that will connect to the new sewer main currently discharge sewage into septic tanks located on each property. The Torres-Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indian tribe has determined that these tanks are failing and have caused seepage of sewage to ground water and in cases sewage has been detected above ground. The proposed project will allow the Tribe to abandon the failing septic tanks and allow them to connect to CVWDs existing sewage treatment system.

Farmers Cooperative Almond Huller was incorporated in 1981 to serve of the almond industry and support local farmers. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist farmers, ranchers, and rural small businesses in developing renewable energy systems, and in making energy-efficiency improvements to their operations. Project funds will be used for the purchase of the 65 gW hydroelectric energy recovery project to produce and export electricity. This project will produce 65,000,000 kWh per year, which is enough electricity to power 7,781 homes per year.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development loan guarantee investment will be used to purchase and make improvements for a new headquarters facility. Surprise Valley Electrification Corp. is located in Alturas, California and serves more than 6,443 customers with over 7,650 miles of line in four counties in California, Oregon, and Nevada.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will help California Rural Water Association (CRWA) purchase four video teleconferencing kits located in four locations across California. The project will include CRWAs Sacramento headquarters as the Hub, connecting to end-user sites in the Fresno, San Bernardino and Imperial Valley regions. The equipment will be used to implement an innovative, centralized remote distance learning model for CRWA to teach students participating in their Water/Wastewater Specialist Apprenticeship Program. This program serves as a pathway for workers employed in the utilities industry to upgrade and enhance their technical, managerial, and financial knowledge and skills in the operation and management of their local utilities.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will help fund the Mariposa County Health & Human Services 2020 Telehealth Project, which will provide telehealth services from three rural hub and end user sites to four end-user fixed sites by providing Telehealth Evaluation carts at the fixed primary hub and end user sites to connect county residents to remote medical services. Seventy laptops will be made available to providers from the primary fixed Hub and End-User site county to serve residents for remote medical evaluations. Laptops will be equipped with the AGNES Connect Software Module. AGNES Connect is a telemedicine platform that enables remote clinical healthcare providers to capture and share medical device data, exchange documents and medical images in real-time, and participate in a live video conference.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will deploy an interactive video conferencing network to help address the need for mental health service. The network will link residents of two rural communities in Imperial County to mental health professionals. These professionals will provide mental health assessments, psychiatric assessment, medication support services, psychotherapy, case management and crisis intervention.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will use synchronous technologies to improve access to education programs addressing substance use disorders, including opioids, expand access to Science Technology Engineering and Math (STEM) education and improve workforce readiness, and improve community sustainability/resilience during national disasters. The Imperial County Office of Education is working in partnership with the El Centro Regional Medical Center, the Imperial County Behavioral Health Services, the Imperial Valley Regional Occupational Program and seven local school districts. This project will serve 22 school sites in eight economically distressed and isolated communities in Imperial County, California.

naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development Investment will be used to cover additional costs associated with constructing a facility for a food closet in Auburn, CA. The Auburn Interfaith Food Closet, Inc. provides food for 700 low-income, homeless and needy families in the Greater Auburn area monthly. The facility will provide greater accessibility for their customers. Owning their own facility as opposed to leasing a facility will ensure expenses remain stable for continued longevity of the organization. The energy efficient building will assist in lower overhead to run the facility. Exceptional community support has contributed to their robust capital campaign which will provide more than half of the project costs for the facility.

project_announced_description: The Rural Development investment will be used to replace the more than 13,000 existing manual read meters with automatic meter reading technology or radio read meters. The districts existing meters are of various ages, condition, and accuracy. They manually read all water meters, which requires the employees to drive to each water meter location, open the lid or cover of the meter box, read the meter and manually enter the reading into a handheld data collector. The district normally only collects meter data six time each year, but snow in portions of the district can prevent meter reads from being collected for as much as six months at a time. This project will allow data to be collected by simply driving in proximity to the meters, so that signals can be transmitted to a receiver in the vehicle allowing for consistent, accurate monthly meter reads for all areas of the district.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase a new first response utility vehicle that will serve the community of Heber, CA. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to repair old, leaking waterlines. The project will install 223 feet of water main line, one fire hydrant, and connect 45 new meters to water main lines. This project will help the Lake of the Woods Mutual Water Company reduce water loss due to leaks and improve service to its users. The water company is contributing $43,268 to this project. Previous funding includes $1 million in Rural Development grants, $1,415,500 from the California Department of Water Resources and $25,732 from the water company.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will assist two communities in Shasta County that were devastated by the Carr Fire during the summer of 2018. The Shasta Community Services District (CSD) and the Keswick County Service Area (CSA) both experienced catastrophic damage from the wildfire. Shasta CSD lost more than 500 homes within its service area reducing their active customers by 62%; and the losses in Keswick CSA were even more devastating with only 10 homes out of 209 remaining after the fire. Both agencies were operating their own water systems prior to the Carr Fire. The continued operation of both water systems is no longer feasible due to the loss of customer base. There is only 2,200 feet separating the two water systems, therefore they plan to consolidate into a single agency and utilize the Shasta CSD Water Treatment Plant to supply water to both service areas. The grant funds will be used to construct a pipeline to interconnect the two water systems and allow the CSD to supply water to the CSA customers. The project will also include fire hydrants, new telemetry, water meters and a rate study needed for the two systems to operate as one.
